reviewers.agent: general-purpose subagent (Opus 4.8), separate context — two adversarial rounds, ran the parser against 30+ real Stripe paths

records.finding: deriveOp leaked unbounded Stripe object ids into the op label of biz_provider_calls_total (ADR-0004 bounded-cardinality violation). First surfaced for namespaced resources (/v1/checkout/sessions/cs_x -> checkout.cs_x); a fix by id-shape was then shown to still leak user-defined all-lowercase ids (/v1/coupons/summer -> coupons.summer.list), which are shape-indistinguishable from resource words.
records.evidence: Round 1: deriveOp(GET,/v1/checkout/sessions/cs_test_abc123) = checkout.cs_test_abc123. Round 2 (against the shape-based fix): deriveOp(GET,/v1/coupons/summer) = coupons.summer.list; deriveOp(GET,/v1/products/my-custom-product) = products.my-custom-product.list.
records.reason: Rewrote deriveOp to strip ids by POSITION (the segment after a resource is always an id, whatever its shape), with a namespace-aware resource span (stripeNamespaces set) so ids under /v1/<ns>/<resource>/<id> land on a drop position, plus an isIDShaped backstop for auto-generated ids from any future namespace not yet in the set. Final adversarial round returned [] across namespaced, user-defined-lowercase, hyphenated, collision, degenerate, and query-string attacks.

records.finding: TestDeriveOp covered only single-segment resources with auto-generated prefix_<digit> ids, so it gave false green: it exercised neither namespaced resources nor user-defined all-lowercase ids — exactly the two path classes that leaked.
records.evidence: Original table had only /v1/payment_intents, /v1/customers/cus_1, /v1/charges, /v1/refunds — no /v1/checkout/sessions/... and no /v1/coupons/<custom>.
records.reason: Added namespaced cases (checkout/sessions, billing_portal/sessions, issuing/cards, customers/sources) and user-defined-id boundedness guards (/v1/coupons/summer, /FREESHIP, /black_friday, /25off, /v1/products/my-custom-product, /v1/plans/gold), each asserting the id is stripped from op.

records.finding: The deriveOp/isStripeID doc comment stated a false universal invariant — that a Stripe id's suffix always carries a digit or uppercase and a resource word never does — which is exactly the wrong assumption that produced the user-defined-id leak.
records.evidence: Comment claimed ids are distinguishable by shape; coupon ids summer/black_friday are ids yet all-lowercase.
records.reason: Comments rewritten to describe position-based stripping and to state honestly that isIDShaped is only a backstop for unknown namespaces, not the primary id test; the documented residual (a future unknown namespace addressing sub-items by a user-defined lowercase id) is accurate and bounded, not a current leak.
